reason: Holds under the project lens. The record's byte 10 (s_ptr+1 on entry to .cells_on_page) is written only at render.6502:1742 by draw_column from its first cell's high byte, which up_cell wraps into &40-&7F (CMP #&40 / ADC #&40); compiled and cached records branch away at BMI compiled before any of this. Each next cell takes 2 or 3 from a value in &40-&7F, giving &3D-&7D; ORA #&40 alone maps &3D-&3F to &7D-&7F and leaves &40-&7D as they are, exactly as AND #&3F / ORA #&40 does. It is also the same arithmetic draw_column's own next cell uses (line 1801), so the restore walks back over the very addresses the draw saved. Flags: C after SBC #&02 is unchanged (AND and ORA leave C alone), and N/Z are overwritten before anything tests them (LDA v_ptr / ADC). Memory and paging are unchanged: the same s_ptr/v_ptr reads and writes, the same ROMSEL and ACCCON state, and nothing is raster-timed. It touches no PROTECTED line, generated source or table. The unreached SKIP 2 after JMP columns keeps .compiled and everything after it at their old addresses, so its room in bank 4 is unchanged. The game plays the same: the screen bytes restored are identical on every path, because the front end, helicopter, game over and completion screen all use this same restore with records drawn by draw_column.
